title: ÆTHER: Yaazhini (Tamil indie-pop name chant with Sufi colour, 1 min test)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

positive_styles: modern Tamil indie-pop love song with a gentle swaying dance pulse, quirky and catchy, viral singalong, a Tamil melodic core with Sufi colour layered on top
mysterious, longing harmonic-minor melody: raga Kiravani in D (D E F G A Bb C#), the melody leans on Bb and C#, small sung slides, simple and singable
chant-like looping refrain built on a girl's name, repeated many times, short punchy lines, the arrangement swells under the chant each time it returns
Sufi colour: harmonium drone and chords, tight handclaps and soft group claps, dholak and tabla groove, a soft bowed string answering the voice
modern indie-pop production: melodic sub bass, snappy modern kick and snap, wide clean mix, intimate and warm, 100 BPM steady
intimate soft young male lead voice, slightly breathy and nasal, laid-back half-sung delivery close to the mic, light modern autotune, cheeky and tender
two young female voices: one sings Sufi-style wordless alaaps with long held notes, the other doubles the refrain softly
harmonium and claps first, the female alaap floats on top, the beat and sub bass enter at the end

brief.notes: Jithesh 3 Nov 08:49 on Semma Paiyan revox: 'We need a Radhimaa type song, this is totally different mode and pathetic'. Fresh start from research on the reference (style only): indie-pop with a modern pulse, Sufi/devotional colours, Tamil melodic core, a chant-like name refrain repeated heavily, intimate lead with female voices. We had been in bright Hamsadhwani with ornamented Carnatic voices: wrong mode. Now harmonic-minor Kiravani D, harmonium/claps/dholak, soft breathy lead, wordless female alaap, original name hook 'Yaazhini'. 60 s test first.

story: A guy who was dumped keeps calling out her name, pretending he is fine while his thumb hovers over her name on his phone.
